diagram_classification: cosmological / astronomical (solar-lunar diagram, probably related to eclipses or lunar phases and the Sun–Moon–Earth relationship)
interpretation: The diagram shows a central dark disc, probably the Earth, surrounded by concentric circles. A graduated outer ring with tick marks acts as a scale for measuring degrees, hours or days. Around the centre run radial lines and a ring of red dots, which may be a division of the circle into equal parts (hours, days or lunar stations). A red-rayed sun with a human face stands at the top. Two crescent moons stand at the left and right, and a ringed dark disc stands at the bottom. Together these figures appear to show the Sun and Moon in different positions relative to the Earth. They may illustrate lunar phases, an eclipse, or the geometry of illumination, with the dark disc at the bottom perhaps standing for a darkened or eclipsed body or for the shadow. The German text at the top mentions an hour ("ein stunde") and says that something is shown "in dieser sper" (in this sphere). This supports reading the diagram as a time-measuring or astronomical figure of the heavens. The exact function of each element, such as the dots, the small star at the left and the red outer rays, remains uncertain.
evidence: A central dark disc is ringed in red. Concentric circles, a tick-marked outer band, radial lines and red dots form a measured scale. A rayed sun with a face is placed at the top. Crescent moons are at the left and right, and a dark ringed disc is at the bottom. Red short rays radiate outward. The vernacular text above mentions an hour and a sphere. The small star at the left and the exact meaning of the dots are uninterpreted.
